title: Ushers, Lobby Attendants, and Ticket Takers
description: Assist patrons at entertainment events by performing duties, such as collecting admission tickets and passes from patrons, assisting in finding seats, searching for lost articles, and helping patrons locate such facilities as restrooms and telephones.

tasks.text: Maintain order and ensure adherence to safety rules.
Examine tickets or passes to verify authenticity, using criteria such as color or date issued.
Verify credentials of patrons desiring entrance into press box and permit only authorized persons to enter.
Refuse admittance to undesirable persons or persons without tickets or passes.
Count and record number of tickets collected.
Clean facilities.
Guide patrons to exits or provide other instructions or assistance in case of emergency.
Assist patrons in finding seats, lighting the way with flashlights, if necessary.
Manage informational kiosks or displays of event signs or posters.
Greet patrons attending entertainment events.
Operate refreshment stands during intermission or obtain refreshments for press box patrons during performances.
Lead tours and answer visitors' questions about the exhibits.
Sell or collect admission tickets, passes, or facility memberships from patrons at entertainment events.
Settle seating disputes or help solve other customer concerns.
Manage inventory or sale of artist merchandise.
Provide assistance with patrons' special needs, such as helping those with wheelchairs.
Assist patrons by giving directions to points in or outside of the facility or providing information about local attractions.
Distribute programs to patrons.
Give door checks to patrons who are temporarily leaving establishments.
Search for lost articles or for parents of lost children.
Work with others to change advertising displays.
Page individuals wanted at the box office.
Schedule or manage staff, such as volunteer usher corps.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Microsoft Word.

skills.name: Optical character reader OCR or scanning software
skills.def: Software to convert an image of text, such as a scanned paper document or electronic fax file, into electronic text which can be edited or used in other applications. Examples: Ticket Alternative Express Entry, Ticket scanning software.
